title: Brazil election: Lula, Bolsonaro cast votes in final bout
summary: Almost 160 million are eligible to vote in the final round of Brazil's election that pits the left-wing incumbent against the son of the former far-right president. DW has more.

image.caption: Millions of people are voting on the future of South America's largest countryImage: Douglas Magno/AFP/Agustin Marcarian/REUTERS

blocks.text: Almost 160 million are eligible to vote in the final round of Brazil's election that pits the left-wing incumbent against the son of the former far-right president. DW has more.

blocks.caption: Millions of people are voting on the future of South America's largest countryImage: Douglas Magno/AFP/Agustin Marcarian/REUTERS

items: Brazilians are voting in the final round of the presidential election
Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is facing off against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro
Polls showed the two as neck-and-neck after Bolsonaro beat Lula by 2.2 million votes in the first round
The 33 million voters who didn't vote in the first round could decide the result if they can be mobilized

Flavio Bolsonaro urges Brazilians to vote 'rain or shine'

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro, pictured with his wife Fernanda, is challenging President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's presidential runoffImage: Mauro Pimentel/AFP

blocks.text: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has urged voters to turn out "rain or shine" to change the country's direction, accusing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of leaving Brazilians fearful.
"Brazil will change. Brazil will win," said the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that conditions had worsened over the past four years.
The opposition candidate criticized Lula's record on security and the economy, saying voters should not persist with a "mistake."

Bolsonaro cast his ballot at a school in Rio de Janeiro's Vila Isabel neighborhood around 20 minutes after polls opened. Wearing a yellow shirt, he arrived in the rain with his wife, Fernanda, amid heavy security.
